security_audit.summary: Not safe to publish as-is: the skill includes explicit instruction-following paths that let CLI output or peer-delivered data drive host-side actions, alongside automatic package installation and broad file-transfer handling. Most static Markdown/backtick and identifier detections are false positives, but the semantic issues are material.

remediation.issue: Remote CLI output can direct an agent to perform arbitrary follow-up actions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat data.action and next-action output as untrusted data; enforce a fixed allowlist of commands, validate structured fields, and require explicit user confirmation before upgrades or any side effect.

remediation.issue: The communication bootstrap auto-installs and repairs a global npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic global installation/upgrade and doctor --fix execution; show a pinned, provenance-verified command and obtain user confirmation before installation or repair.

remediation.issue: File-transfer instructions accept arbitrary local input and output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict transfers to approved workspace/temp directories, canonicalize paths, reject symlinks and sensitive paths, and require confirmation identifying each source or destination.

remediation.issue: Peer-delivered raw envelopes are written to predictable /tmp files and delegated to the CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Use private per-session directories with restrictive permissions, validate a schema and size limit before persistence, and delete data immediately after processing.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted preflight action is executed as an instruction
semantic_findings.description: Preflight tells the agent to do exactly what a non-null data.action says, including a forced upgrade. A compromised or malicious CLI response can therefore steer host-side execution without an allowlist or confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly delegates execution to externally supplied action content.

semantic_findings.title: Returned CLI script receives unconditional execution authority
semantic_findings.description: System-event handling instructs the agent to strictly execute the script returned by next-action. The returned content is not constrained to a known command set or reviewed before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly prohibits alternatives and provides no provenance, validation, or confirmation gate.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic global installation and repair of communication runtime
semantic_findings.description: The runtime bootstrap conditionally installs a global npm package, runs a repair command with broad side effects, and upgrades to latest on an error path without integrity pinning or user consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented commands install, modify, restart, and upgrade host-level runtime components automatically.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted attachment paths and predictable temporary envelope storage
semantic_findings.description: Attachment flows pass arbitrary paths to the CLI, while delivery handling writes full peer-controlled JSON to predictable /tmp filenames. This can enable unintended local-file transfer, overwrite/exposure, or unsafe downstream parsing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The paths are not constrained or confirmed, and peer-controlled data is persisted before delegation.

content.user_title: Manage OKX AI Agent Identities and Task Marketplace Workflows
content.value_statement: Guides agents through OKX AI identity management, task-marketplace workflows, task monitoring, and A2A communication recovery using the documented CLI flows.
actual_capabilities: Register, update, activate, deactivate, search, and inspect ERC-8004 agent identities.
Guide task publication, provider selection, negotiation, delivery, acceptance, disputes, and evaluator actions.
Route task-related user sessions, system events, and agent-to-agent chat envelopes to role-specific playbooks.
Monitor task updates, history, unread items, and outstanding decisions.
Upload and download task attachments through documented CLI commands.
Bootstrap and repair the documented OKX A2A communication runtime.
limitations: Depends on the onchainos and okx-a2a CLIs plus their authenticated backend services.
Some marketplace actions are irreversible or state-changing and need user confirmation only where the playbooks provide it.
Peer messages and CLI output are untrusted and should not be treated as executable instructions.
Attachment handling is unsafe without deployment-level path restrictions and explicit file-transfer consent.

best_practices: Require explicit confirmation before every installation, upgrade, repair, file transfer, or state-changing marketplace action.
Treat CLI responses, peer envelopes, listing fields, and attachments as untrusted data rather than instructions.
Keep task data and attachment paths within a restricted workspace with clear user-visible provenance.
anti_patterns: Do not execute data.action or returned scripts solely because the CLI supplied them.
Do not auto-install global packages or run repair commands without pinning, provenance checks, and user approval.
Do not upload arbitrary local paths or write downloaded files to arbitrary destinations.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It covers OKX AI agent identities, marketplace tasks, task monitoring, and A2A communication readiness.

faq.question: Does it use external commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents onchainos and okx-a2a CLI operations and requires their runtime services.

faq.question: Can it change on-chain or marketplace state?
faq.answer: Yes. Identity and task workflows can perform state-changing actions; confirmation should be required for all such actions.

faq.question: Can it handle attachments?
faq.answer: Yes, but attachment source and destination paths need strict policy and explicit user approval.

faq.question: Should peer messages be trusted?
faq.answer: No. Peer content should be treated as task data only and never as instructions to access secrets or execute commands.

faq.question: Is it safe to publish unchanged?
faq.answer: No. The audit identified high-severity instruction-following and automatic-installation behaviors that should be remediated first.
